---
title: "Annotations are measurements"
---

[Şahin and Adalı (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10579-017-9390-y) describe the ITU/IMST Turkish PropBank: predicate-specific frames were paired with argument candidates from the IMST dependency treebank, Turkish-speaking crowd workers selected plain-language role descriptions, and unresolved cases were adjudicated. The [official project release](https://turkishpropbank.github.io/) provides the frames, crowd layers, and final annotations. The course extract is privacy-sanitized from the [pinned project repository](https://github.com/turkishpropbank/turkishpropbank.github.io/tree/5cd9c9918c8a7f4fd62802387e04d14b995ecb66); it removes platform identifiers, locations, timestamps, and free text.

The project site states that resources built in the project are distributed under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, while the repository's short license header names the Turkish frame files specifically. We use the derived table for this noncommercial course under the project-wide statement and retain that scope qualification.

This release supplies an empirical bridge from annotation to measurement. One row records whether one worker's selected description matches the final adjudicated description. Agreement with adjudication is observed. The validity of the adjudicated description is not.

## Loading individual judgments

```{r}
#| label: load-turkish-propbank
#| message: false
#| warning: false

turkish <- utils::read.csv(
  "data/turkish-propbank/role-agreement-judgments.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(turkish) == 55207L,
  length(unique(turkish$item_id)) == 18306L,
  length(unique(turkish$worker_id)) == 144L,
  setequal(unique(turkish$correct), 0:1),
  sum(turkish$correct) == 46078L,
  !anyDuplicated(paste(
    turkish$item_id,
    turkish$judgment_index,
    sep = "::"
  ))
)

turkish_analysis <- subset(
  turkish,
  role_group %in% c("core", "adjunct")
)
turkish_analysis$role_group <- stats::relevel(
  factor(turkish_analysis$role_group),
  ref = "core"
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(turkish_analysis) == 52784L,
  length(unique(turkish_analysis$item_id)) == 17502L,
  length(unique(turkish_analysis$worker_id)) == 144L,
  sum(turkish_analysis$role_group == "core") == 36672L,
  sum(turkish_analysis$role_group == "adjunct") == 16112L
)
```

The binary response is

$$
Y_{ij}=
\begin{cases}
1 & \text{worker }j\text{ selected item }i\text{'s adjudicated description},\\
0 & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

A zero is a recorded disagreement, not a missing response. It also does not establish that the worker is wrong in an independent linguistic sense, because the comparison target is the project's adjudication.

## Keeping three agreement quantities distinct

The paper reports Cohen's $\kappa=.936$ for an expert versus trust-weighted aggregate answers on 2,000 deliberately unambiguous test questions. It reports Fleiss' $\kappa=.65$ across varying workers on roughly 18,000 ordinary multi-category questions. The response above is a third quantity: an individual worker's binary match with the later adjudicated description. The three quantities have different observational units and denominators.

This lesson asks whether individual agreement differs between predicate-specific core descriptions and general adjunct-like descriptions. The **adjudication-agreement target (AAT)** is thus a property of this released task, not a worker-competence score and not a replication of either $\kappa$ statistic.

## Raw agreement by adjudicated role class

```{r}
#| label: summarize-turkish-propbank

turkish_raw <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(split(turkish_analysis, turkish_analysis$role_group), function(d) {
    agreements <- sum(d$correct)
    judgments <- nrow(d)
    interval <- stats::binom.test(agreements, judgments)$conf.int
    data.frame(
      role_group = as.character(unique(d$role_group)),
      judgments = judgments,
      agreements = agreements,
      raw_probability = agreements / judgments,
      raw_lower = interval[[1]],
      raw_upper = interval[[2]]
    )
  })
)
rownames(turkish_raw) <- NULL

knitr::kable(turkish_raw, digits = 3)
```

The raw proportions retain every individual judgment but do not account for repeated items or workers. Items may differ in difficulty, and workers may differ in response behavior.

## Fitting a crossed measurement model

Let $u_i$ be an item intercept and $v_j$ a worker intercept. The model is

$$
Y_{ij}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\pi_{ij}),
$$

$$
\operatorname{logit}(\pi_{ij})
=\beta_0+\beta_1\operatorname{Adjunct}_i+u_i+v_j,
$$

$$
u_i\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma_{\text{item}}^2),
\qquad
v_j\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma_{\text{worker}}^2).
$$

The fixed contrast compares adjudicated role classes at zero-valued item and worker intercepts. The crossed terms retain the repeated-measurement structure.

```{r}
#| label: fit-turkish-propbank
#| message: false
#| warning: false

turkish_control <- lme4::glmerControl(
  optimizer = "bobyqa",
  optCtrl = list(maxfun = 200000)
)

turkish_baseline <- lme4::glmer(
  correct ~ 1 + (1 | item_id) + (1 | worker_id),
  data = turkish_analysis,
  family = stats::binomial(),
  control = turkish_control
)

turkish_role_model <- lme4::glmer(
  correct ~ role_group + (1 | item_id) + (1 | worker_id),
  data = turkish_analysis,
  family = stats::binomial(),
  control = turkish_control
)

turkish_comparison <- stats::anova(
  turkish_baseline,
  turkish_role_model,
  test = "Chisq"
)
turkish_fixed <- lme4::fixef(turkish_role_model)

stopifnot(
  is.null(turkish_role_model@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages),
  !lme4::isSingular(turkish_role_model, tol = 1e-4)
)

turkish_design <- stats::model.matrix(
  ~ role_group,
  data.frame(
    role_group = factor(
      c("core", "adjunct"),
      levels = c("core", "adjunct")
    )
  )
)
turkish_vcov <- as.matrix(stats::vcov(turkish_role_model))
turkish_eta <- as.vector(turkish_design %*% turkish_fixed)
turkish_eta_se <- sqrt(diag(
  turkish_design %*% turkish_vcov %*% t(turkish_design)
))
turkish_fitted <- data.frame(
  role_group = c("core", "adjunct"),
  fitted_probability = stats::plogis(turkish_eta),
  fitted_lower = stats::plogis(turkish_eta - 1.96 * turkish_eta_se),
  fitted_upper = stats::plogis(turkish_eta + 1.96 * turkish_eta_se)
)
turkish_summary <- merge(
  turkish_raw,
  turkish_fitted,
  by = "role_group",
  sort = FALSE
)

model_result <- data.frame(
  quantity = c(
    "Adjunct versus core coefficient",
    "Likelihood-ratio chi-square",
    "Likelihood-ratio degrees of freedom"
  ),
  value = c(
    unname(turkish_fixed[["role_groupadjunct"]]),
    turkish_comparison$Chisq[[2]],
    turkish_comparison$Df[[2]]
  )
)

knitr::kable(model_result, digits = 3)
```

## Showing raw and fitted agreement together

```{r}
#| label: plot-turkish-propbank
#| fig-width: 6.1
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| fig-cap: "Individual agreement with adjudication. Raw proportions use exact binomial intervals; fitted probabilities condition on zero item and worker intercepts."

turkish_plot_data <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    role_group = turkish_summary$role_group,
    estimate = turkish_summary$raw_probability,
    lower = turkish_summary$raw_lower,
    upper = turkish_summary$raw_upper,
    estimate_type = "Raw"
  ),
  data.frame(
    role_group = turkish_summary$role_group,
    estimate = turkish_summary$fitted_probability,
    lower = turkish_summary$fitted_lower,
    upper = turkish_summary$fitted_upper,
    estimate_type = "Crossed model"
  )
)
turkish_plot_data$role_group <- factor(
  turkish_plot_data$role_group,
  levels = c("core", "adjunct")
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
  turkish_plot_data,
  ggplot2::aes(role_group, estimate, color = estimate_type)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_errorbar(
    ggplot2::aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
    width = 0.08,
    position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.25)
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    size = 2.4,
    position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.25)
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Raw" = "grey35", "Crossed model" = "steelblue4")
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0.6, 1),
    labels = scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1) # dqr-allow: algorithm-setting
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Adjudicated role class",
    y = "Agreement with adjudicated description",
    color = NULL
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top"
  )
```

Individual judgments agree with adjudicated core descriptions more often than with adjunct-like descriptions in this extract. The teaching contrast collapses the paper's multi-category role inventory into two release-based groups. It does not reproduce the paper's agreement calculations, estimate worker competence, or validate the final label. Numbered core roles also remain predicate-specific rather than universal thematic categories.

::: {.callout-note title="Check the measurement target"}
1. What event makes `correct` equal to one?
2. Why is this response not the paper's Cohen or Fleiss $\kappa$?
3. Which repeated units enter the crossed model?
4. Why is the fitted probability not a worker-competence estimate?
:::
